MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Service

PATIENT DETAILS
Patient 1: [redacted name] (Mother)
DOB: [redacted date]
Lab ID: [redacted ID]

Patient 2: [redacted name] (Father)
DOB: [redacted date]
Lab ID: [redacted ID]

Date of Report: [redacted date]
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Referral Date: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) carrier testing requested for both parents following diagnosis of SMA in their child. The affected child has been confirmed to have homozygous deletion of SMN1 exons 7 and 8.

CLINICAL INFORMATION
The couple's first child was diagnosed with SMA Type 1 at 4 months of age following presentation with progressive weakness and hypotonia. Genetic testing confirmed homozygous deletion of SMN1 exons 7 and 8. Parents are seeking carrier status confirmation and genetic counseling regarding recurrence risk for future pregnancies.

METHODOLOGY
Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA) analysis was performed using the GenePro P021 kit to determine SMN1 exon 7 and exon 8 copy number. This assay detects deletions and duplications of the SMN1 gene and can distinguish between SMN1 and the highly homologous SMN2 gene. DNA was extracted from peripheral blood samples using standard protocols. The MLPA reaction products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis and copy number determined by comparison to control samples.

RESULTS

Patient 1 (Mother):
SMN1 Exon 7: 1 copy detected (Normal: 2 copies)
SMN1 Exon 8: 1 copy detected (Normal: 2 copies)
SMN2 copy number: 2 copies

Patient 2 (Father):
SMN1 Exon 7: 1 copy detected (Normal: 2 copies)
SMN1 Exon 8: 1 copy detected (Normal: 2 copies)
SMN2 copy number: 1 copy

Quality metrics: All control probes showed expected ratios. Sample quality adequate.

SUMMARY
Both parents show heterozygous deletion of SMN1 exons 7 and 8, confirming carrier status for Spinal Muscular Atrophy. This finding is consistent with the homozygous deletion identified in their affected child.

The carrier frequency for SMA in the general population is approximately 1 in 40-60. With both parents confirmed as carriers, the recurrence risk for each future pregnancy is:
- 25% affected with SMA
- 50% carrier
- 25% unaffected non-carrier

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss reproductive options and recurrence risks
2. Prenatal diagnosis by MLPA testing is available for future pregnancies from 11 weeks gestation via chorionic villus sampling or from 15 weeks via amniocentesis
3. Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT-M) is also available
4. Carrier testing can be offered to extended family members (siblings of both parents have a 50% risk of being carriers)
5. SMN2 copy number has been determined as this can influence phenotype severity if prenatal testing identifies an affected fetus

This test has been performed in an accredited laboratory (ISO 15189).

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
